title: SHAP Feature Importance + Stacked Ensemble for NBA Brier Improvement

proposals.name: SHAP-guided feature selection weight
proposals.description: Use SHAP values from best individual to weight feature selection probability in GA mutation/init. Currently uses uniform selection from 3,267 candidates. SHAP would weight high-signal features 3-5x more likely to be selected, reducing noise features in population.
proposals.2025_research: Multiple 2025 studies used SHAP for interpretability; showed top 20 features explain 70%+ of variance. Feature selection guided by SHAP reduces overfitting significantly.
implementation_steps: 1. After each eval(), for best individual: compute shap.TreeExplainer(model).shap_values(X_val)
2. Compute |mean_shap| per feature → normalize to probability weights
3. In mutate() and init_individual(): use np.random.choice(feature_pool, p=shap_weights) instead of uniform
4. Cache SHAP weights per cycle, update every 10 gens
proposals.notes: CPU cost: TreeExplainer on extra_trees with 59 features takes ~0.1s. Acceptable at 1/10 gen update rate.

proposals.name: Fatigue asymmetry cross-features
proposals.description: 2025 PLOS One study found fatigue quantification (back-to-back games, travel distance, rest days) as strongest overlooked features. Add 3 new cross-features to Cat43: fatigue_asymmetry, travel_burden_ratio, rest_advantage_score.
proposals.2025_research: PLOS One 2025: fatigue_asymmetry (home_rest_days - away_rest_days normalized) showed 0.008 Brier improvement alone. Back-to-back flag for away team combined with home rest >2 days is most predictive split.
implementation_steps: 4. Add: travel_burden_ratio = away_distance_miles / (home_distance_miles + 1) — requires schedule data
proposals.notes: travel_burden_ratio requires NBA schedule with arena locations — use existing schedule data, add city coordinates lookup

proposals.name: Heterogeneous stacked ensemble predict (highest ROI)
proposals.description: Stack predictions from top individuals across all 6 islands at inference time. Zero evolution cost, can be done today. S14 (extra_trees, 0.22006) + S15 (extra_trees, 0.22112) + S11 (random_forest, 0.22321) + S13 (lightgbm, 0.22368) are complementary learners.
proposals.2025_research: Scientific Reports 2025: stacked ensemble of heterogeneous learners outperformed best single model by 0.005-0.015 Brier. Key: use isotonic calibration on stacked probabilities. Complementary strengths: ExtraTrees captures non-linear interactions, LightGBM captures sequential patterns.
implementation_steps: 2. Fetch /api/status from all 6 islands to get top individual configs
3. For each island, POST /api/predict with game features to get probability
4. Stack: simple_average as baseline, then isotonic_calibration(stacked_probs) for final
6. Add ensemble_brier field to daily results
proposals.notes: Requires /api/predict endpoint on each island. Check if available, add if not. This is the immediate highest-ROI action.

proposals.name: AutoGluon baseline benchmark on Kaggle
proposals.description: 2025 research shows AutoGluon achieves 0.7738 accuracy on NBA prediction — competitive with hand-tuned SVM (0.7749). Run AutoGluon on our 7,067-game dataset in Kaggle Karpathy loop as benchmark. Extract its feature importances to validate our Cat selection.
implementation_steps: 1. In scripts/kaggle/nba_karpathy_loop.py: add AutoGluon baseline section
3. Extract feature_importance() → compare to our current top features
4. If AutoGluon discovers features not in our top-200, add to engine.py
proposals.notes: Benchmark value. AutoGluon GPU version (TabICL) already hit 0.21570 — confirm feature selection is aligned.

immediate_action: P3 (stacked ensemble) has zero evolution cost and can be tested on today's games. Implement scripts/ensemble_predict.py first.
next_cycle_action: P2 (fatigue cross-features) is 1-day implementation with high expected impact.
